intro: Open the ChatGPT Mac app, click More in the sidebar, choose GPTs, then click My GPTs and open the GPT you want. Pin it by clicking its name at the top of the chat, and know that custom GPTs retire on December 11, 2026.
tldr: You can still open an existing custom GPT in the ChatGPT Mac app.
OpenAI's help text says new custom GPTs cannot be built on a personal account.
Go to More, then GPTs, then My GPTs. Pin a GPT by clicking its name at the top of the chat.
Custom GPTs retire on December 11, 2026. Creators can try Migrate to plugin if the option appears.

blocks.text: Here is the honest starting point. As of November 9, 2026, you can still open a custom GPT you already have in the ChatGPT Mac app. You cannot build a new one on a personal account. OpenAI's help text says creation and publishing are limited to managed workspaces where allowed. The help page would not load for this check, so that line rests on search result text.
Why you cannot build a new custom GPT anymore

OpenAI announced the retirement on September 11, 2026. The plan ends custom GPTs on December 11, 2026, and it points creators toward plugins instead. Timing can vary by account and workspace, so treat these dates as the public schedule, not a promise for your account.

If you try to make a new GPT, you may see a Create Plugin Instead option. That is the clearest sign the old route is closed for you. Reports also disagree on the exact cutoff for creating new GPTs. The sources I could open do not agree on one date, so do not plan around a single day.
Find your GPTs in the ChatGPT Mac app

The current Mac app launched on July 9, 2026, for macOS and Windows. It puts Chat, Work, and Codex in one desktop app, and it is available on every plan, including Free. The older native app is renamed ChatGPT Classic, and it shuts down on January 30, 2027.

The steps in this guide come from a June 2026 third-party guide. That guide describes the desktop web version and does not name a macOS version. OpenAI's own help pages returned errors, so I could not confirm its exact menu names. If your screen uses different words, follow the same order and look for the closest match.
Pin a custom GPT to the sidebar

Pinning saves you from searching each time. A pinned GPT sits under a Pinned section in the sidebar, so you can open it in one click. Pinning only changes where the GPT appears. It does not change the instructions or files the creator set up.

Here is a worked example. Say you have a GPT that turns pasted meeting transcripts into notes. You pin it on Monday. On Tuesday you click it in the Pinned section, paste a new transcript, and send. You skip the search, and the GPT behaves the same as before.
Get good answers from a custom GPT

A custom GPT follows the instructions its creator wrote. It may also use files or actions the creator added. Your prompt still shapes the result. Name the task, paste the material, and say what shape you want back, such as a table or a short summary.

Start a new chat for each job. A long chat carries old context into new work, and that can change the answer. If a GPT starts drifting, copy the good parts of the reply into a fresh chat and continue there.
Migrate a custom GPT you made to a plugin

Migration is the path OpenAI names for creators. Open My GPTs, find the GPT under Created by me, and select Migrate to plugin. After migration, the original becomes read-only, so you cannot edit it. Test the plugin before you rely on it.

Only the creator, a workspace owner, or an admin can migrate a GPT. The GPT must be published. Shared access alone is not enough, and plugins must be enabled on the account. If you only use a GPT someone else made, you have nothing to migrate.
What carries over and what does not

items: Custom actions do not transfer, so you may need to rebuild them.
Conversation starters do not transfer one to one.
The model you picked does not carry over.
Bulk migration does not copy sharing settings.

blocks.text: Migrated plugins start private, and your old sharing settings do not come along. OpenAI warns that a migrated plugin may respond differently. Run a few prompts you used before and compare the answers side by side. Adjust the instructions if the tone or length has shifted.

The option may not appear on your account yet. OpenAI has not published a date for when migration opens on each plan. If you cannot see it, you cannot force it. Keep a saved copy of your instructions and files until it shows up, or until the retirement date forces the choice.

blocks.text: Campus Technology and Virtualization Review name only Enterprise workspaces. The Paperless Agent says the retirement covers all plans, including Free, Plus, and Team. I could not confirm the all-plans claim from OpenAI's own page. Check any notice from OpenAI in your account, or ask your workspace admin if you use a work account.
Qualifying Enterprise customers with approved deferrals can keep Custom GPTs running until February 11, 2027. A deferral needs approval, so do not assume you have one.
Mistakes people make with custom GPTs on Mac

items: Searching for voice in the Mac app. Voice left the macOS desktop app effective January 15, 2026. It stays on web, iOS, Android, and Windows.
Expecting a migrated plugin to be shared. Migrated plugins start private, and sharing does not carry over.
Assuming custom actions move with the GPT. They do not, and they may need a rebuild.
Deleting the original before testing the plugin. Keep it until the new version works the way you need.
Following an old Mac guide. The Mac Install Guide predates the July 2026 app and does not mention GPTs.
Looking for GPTs on the chatgpt.com homepage. Its navigation lists New chat, Images, Deep research, Settings, and Plugins, with no GPTs entry.

blocks.text: If you only want a standing tone or background for your chats, custom instructions may cover it. The steps are in [How to set custom instructions in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/set-custom-instructions-in-chatgpt). For a set of files tied to one project, see [How to create a project in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/create-a-project-in-chatgpt).
What to do before December 11, 2026

Start with a list. Open My GPTs and write down every GPT you use. Mark which ones you created and which someone shared with you. You cannot migrate a GPT you did not create, so those need a different plan.
Next, copy each GPT's instructions into a plain text file. Save the names of any knowledge files and the starter prompts. Starter prompts do not move one to one, so keep your own copies.

Then, for each GPT you made, check whether Migrate to plugin appears. If it does, migrate one GPT, test it with your usual work, and only then move on to the next. If it does not appear, keep your saved copy and test a rebuilt version in a project or a normal chat.
The main risk is a plan made too late. A GPT that worked well in October may respond differently after a move. Give yourself time to compare outputs before the date, and keep notes on what changed.

faq.question: Can I still create a new custom GPT in ChatGPT on Mac?
faq.answer: On a personal account, OpenAI's help text says new GPT creation and publishing are not available. Creation is limited to managed workspaces where allowed. If you try, you may see Create Plugin Instead. Ask your workspace admin what your team can still do.

faq.question: Where do I find my custom GPTs in the Mac app?
faq.answer: Click More in the sidebar, choose GPTs, then click My GPTs. Open the GPT from that list. These steps come from a June 2026 third-party guide, so match the labels to what you see on screen.

faq.question: How do I pin a custom GPT so it stays in the sidebar?
faq.answer: Open the GPT, click its name at the top of the chat, and choose Pin. The GPT then appears under the Pinned section. Pinning does not change the GPT's instructions or files.

faq.question: When do custom GPTs stop working?
faq.answer: OpenAI schedules the retirement for December 11, 2026. Sources disagree on which plans it covers. Enterprise-focused reports name only Enterprise workspaces, while one third-party site says all plans. Check your account notices.

faq.question: Does migrating keep my GPT's instructions and files?
faq.answer: Instructions, knowledge files, and connected apps carry over. Custom actions do not, and conversation starters do not move one to one. The selected model also does not carry over, so check it after the move.

faq.question: Why can't I see Migrate to plugin?
faq.answer: The option may not be open on your account yet, and OpenAI has not published a date for each plan. You must be the creator, a workspace owner, or an admin. The GPT must be published, and plugins must be enabled.

faq.question: Can I use voice with custom GPTs in the Mac app?
faq.answer: Not in the macOS desktop app. Voice mode left that app effective January 15, 2026, and it stays on web, iOS, Android, and Windows, according to 9to5Mac.

faq.question: Is the old ChatGPT Mac app still available?
faq.answer: The old native app is renamed ChatGPT Classic. It shuts down on January 30, 2027, with no extension planned. Use the new desktop app for your work from now on.

task: Find, pin and plan custom GPTs in ChatGPT on Mac
appliesTo: ChatGPT desktop app for macOS, as of November 2026
requirements: An account that can already see your existing custom GPTs
The ChatGPT desktop app for Mac, updated to the version with Chat, Work, and Codex
For migration: you must be the creator, a workspace owner, or an admin, and the GPT must be published
Plugins enabled on the account, if you plan to migrate

steps.name: Open the ChatGPT app
steps.text: Open ChatGPT from the Dock or from Applications. If you see Chat, Work, and Codex, you are in the new desktop app that launched on July 9, 2026.
steps.tip: If you still see the old layout, check for updates and relaunch. The old app is renamed ChatGPT Classic.

steps.name: Find More in the sidebar
steps.text: Look at the left sidebar. Click More, the item marked with three dots.

steps.name: Open GPTs
steps.text: Choose GPTs from the More list. This opens Explore GPTs.
steps.tip: If GPTs is missing from the menu, see the troubleshooting list below.

steps.name: Click My GPTs
steps.text: On Explore GPTs, click My GPTs. This is the list where your own GPTs appear.

steps.name: Open the GPT
steps.text: Click the GPT you want. It opens in a chat that uses that GPT's instructions.

steps.name: Send your prompt
steps.text: Type in the message box at the bottom of the chat. Press Return to send. The GPT replies using the instructions its creator set.

steps.name: Click the GPT name
steps.text: At the top of the chat, click the GPT's name to open its options.

steps.name: Choose Pin
steps.text: In that menu, choose Pin. The GPT moves into the Pinned section of the sidebar.
steps.tip: The pin steps come from a guide that describes the desktop web version. If Pin is missing, update the app and try again.

steps.name: Confirm the Pinned section
steps.text: Look in the sidebar for the Pinned section. Your GPT should appear there. Click it to open the GPT in one step.

steps.name: Find the GPT you made
steps.text: If you created the GPT, open My GPTs again and look under Created by me.

steps.name: Select Migrate to plugin
steps.text: Select Migrate to plugin next to the GPT. Only the creator, a workspace owner, or an admin can do this, and the GPT must be published.
steps.tip: If the option is missing, your account may not have migration yet. OpenAI has not published a date for each plan.

steps.name: Review what carried over
steps.text: Check the new plugin's instructions, knowledge files, and connected apps. Rebuild any custom actions, since they do not transfer.

steps.name: Test with real work
steps.text: Run a few prompts you used before. Compare the answers and adjust the instructions if the tone or length changed.

steps.name: Save a copy before December 11, 2026
steps.text: Keep a plain text copy of each GPT's instructions, file names, and starter prompts. Do this before the retirement date, because starter prompts do not transfer one to one.

troubleshooting.problem: More is missing from the sidebar
troubleshooting.fix: Check that the sidebar is open and not filtered. Quit the app with ⌘Q, reopen it, and look again. If More is still missing, confirm you are in the new desktop app.
You may not have created or saved any GPTs on this account. Check which account you are signed in to. A GPT made on one account does not appear on another.

troubleshooting.problem: Pin does not show up in the sidebar
troubleshooting.fix: Click the GPT name at the top of the chat again and look for Pin. If the menu looks different on your Mac, update the app and check again.

troubleshooting.problem: Create Plugin Instead appears when I try to make a GPT
troubleshooting.fix: This is the expected result for new creation on a personal account. Plugins are the replacement path. A workspace admin can tell you what your team can still open.

troubleshooting.problem: A GPT answers differently after migration
troubleshooting.fix: OpenAI warns that migrated plugins may respond differently. Compare outputs with your saved prompts and adjust the instructions. Check the model setting, since the selected model does not carry over.

troubleshooting.problem: Typing @ does not bring up my GPT
troubleshooting.fix: An older community thread describes typing @ to reach pinned GPTs. I saw that tip only in a search result, so test it before you rely on it.
